paper_id: Preserving Knowledge in Large Language Model with Model-Agnostic Self-Decompression
title: Preserving Knowledge in Large Language Model with Model-Agnostic Self-Decompression
motivation: LLMs/MLLMs suffer catastrophic forgetting when fine-tuned on domain-specific data; language benchmarks degrade during SFT while vision-language benchmarks improve.
problem_framing: Framing LLMs as lossless compressors; model forgetting represents compressed knowledge being overwritten; decompression via synthetic data generation can recover it.
key_insight: Treating text generation from LLMs as a 'self-decompression' process preserves original knowledge by using LLMs as offline data generators to dump training corpus.
method_signature: Tree Generation (TG-SFT): layered tree expansion with alternating user/assistant roles, semantic deduplication, tunable N_i branching factors per layer.
evaluation_criteria: LLM benchmark restoration (should match original backbone score 53.41); MLLM benchmark maintenance; comparison with human-generated ShareGPT data.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Math domain synthesis produced wrong calculations and simple derivations; SFT with math data caused noticeable benchmark degradation. No universal benchmark exists for synthetic data quality evaluation.
evidence_for_taste: 模型已经开始遗忘其通用语言能力
合成数据接近人类数据质量
MLLM benchmarks grew, but LLM benchmarks started to deteriorate
LLMs not only excel in text compression but also show competitive performance
synthetic data may include many inaccurate facts
LLMs tend to generate simple/wrong calculations and derivations
thinking_moves: 将LLM视为无损压缩器，用'解压'视角重新定义知识保持问题
用实验观察区分过拟合与遗忘：MLLM性能上升但LLM性能下降说明遗忘而非仅过拟合
通过tree结构控制生成多样性与深度，而非随机采样
承认合成数据的局限性（数学领域质量不足），而非夸大方法通用性
